title: Compact toolchain manifests and preserve-environment lint shim
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce CI init time and flakes caused by toolchain divergence while supporting developer workflows that rely on preserved environment variables during local lint runs. This PR collapses the monolithic toolchain manifests into small, stage-aware manifests and adds a lightweight 'preserve-env' lint shim so dev environments do not lose PATH/KUBECONFIG/KMS_* during presubmit steps. Changes are backward-compatible and guarded behind a feature flag for the release rollout.

Summary of changes: consolidated toolchain manifests into 'toolchain/manifests/{ci,dev,release}.yaml', introduced 'ci/presubmit/preserve-env-lint-adapter' (bash shim + minimal node harness) to wrap existing linters without reinitializing environment, added tests and smoke workflows, updated GitHub Actions matrix to prefer compact manifests and a seeded cache-key for faster bootstrap. Also updated docs/ci/tooling.md with migration notes and a short rollback recipe.
commits: Init compact manifests and shim (Asha Patel); add preserve-env adapter tests and CI smoke (Asha Patel); update workflows to reference stage-aware manifests (Gabriel Chen); add docs and release notes (Marta Novak); fix flaky windows path handling in shim (Asha Patel)

review_comments: Gabriel Chen (2026-02-22): Nice separation of manifests. Two asks: 1) can we avoid changing package.json at root in this PR (split into dep-only)? 2) please add a smoke job that runs preserve-env shim on macOS -- CI flakiness is primarily mac-specific.
Asha Patel (2026-02-23): Split node dep bump into follow-up (will open ENG-4201). Added macOS smoke job and updated tests to cover mac path handling.

Marta Novak (2026-02-25): Found race where bootstrap.sh reinitializes PATH; request: guard PATH reset behind TOOLCHAIN_INIT=false. Also please add migration note for customers running Dedicated which pin toolchain manifests.
Asha Patel (2026-02-26): Added TOOLCHAIN_INIT guard and migration doc section; expanded release notes with rollback recipe. Ready for final review.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): Approved after CI green and docs look good. Left a minor comment on wording in tooling.md which I will not block on.
ci_checks_summary: Checks: unit (pass), integration-smoke (pass), e2e-nightly (skipped on feature flag), lint (pass), static-checks (pass), dependency-scan (pass)
release_notes:
- Introduce compact stage-aware toolchain manifests (toolchain/manifests/{ci,dev,release}.yaml) to reduce CI bootstrap time and improve cacheability.
- Add 'preserve-env' lint shim to avoid losing developer environment variables during local and CI lint runs.
- Docs: migration and rollback instructions added to docs/ci/migration.md.
- Backward compatible; rollout gated by feature flag 'compact_toolchain=true'.
notes_for_releasers: Feature flag enabled by default in CI after one-week canary. For enterprise/private customers that pinned manifests, coordinate change with on-prem installer team (see ENG-3421). If rollback needed: re-enable legacy manifests by setting compact_toolchain=false in repo-level ci config and revert the adapter usage in workflows.
testing_instructions: 1) checkout branch and run ./scripts/ci/bootstrap.sh --manifest toolchain/manifests/dev.yaml; 2) run tests/preserve-env/test_local_lint.sh on mac/linux/windows; 3) trigger .github/workflows/presubmit-smoke.yaml via workflow_dispatch; verify env vars (PATH, KUBECONFIG, KMS_KEY) persist across shim boundary.
long_term_followups:
- ENG-4201: split dependency bumps for root package.json into independent PR.
- ENG-4300: extend preserve-env shim to support agent-managed HSM env variables.
- ENG-4422: telemetry to measure reduction in CI cold-start time.
human_readable_summary: This PR trims CI bootstrap time by reorganizing toolchain manifests and introduces a small shim that preserves developer environment variables during lint steps, reducing CI flakes and lowering the barrier for local dev parity. Merged via squash after reviewers approved and CI passed.
